q: The Tamil Poet and Author of Ramayana in Tamil Kamban was in the court of which Kings?
explanation: Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana (Ramavataram) at the court of the Chola king Kulottunga III, not under the Hoysalas, Pandyas or Cheras.

q: What was the mother tongue of the Devagiri Yadavas?
explanation: The Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri ruled Maharashtra and their mother tongue was Marathi, which they encouraged; Sanskrit was only the language of scholarship. Telugu was the Kakatiyas' language, Kannada the Hoysalas'.

notes.text: - **Mother tongue:** **Marathi** (APPSC G2 2000; APPSC PYQ) – not Telugu, Kannada or Urdu; the Yadavas **encouraged Marathi**; **Sanskrit** = language of scholarship (not Telugu at court).

q: Mother tongue of the Devagiri Yadavas?
explanation: The Devagiri (Seuna) Yadavas ruled present-day Maharashtra and their mother tongue was Marathi; they patronised Marathi literature (Dnyaneshwari, Lilacharitra). Telugu, Kannada and Urdu do not fit.

notes.text: - **Mother tongue:** **Marathi** (APPSC G2 2000; APPSC PYQ) – not Telugu, Kannada or Urdu; the Yadavas **encouraged Marathi**; **Sanskrit** = language of scholarship (not Telugu at court).

q: Among the following who established Devagiri as an independent Yadava Kingdom?
explanation: Bhillama V threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule, declared independence and built Devagiri (c. 1187) as the Yadava capital. Prola I, Prola II and Ganapati were Kakatiya rulers.

notes.text: - **Founder of the independent kingdom:** **Bhillama V** threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule and built **Devagiri** (c. **1187**) as capital (APPSC G2 2000) – not Prola I, Prola II or Ganapati (Kakatiyas), not Shankaradeva.

q: Which Yadava king defeated Rudradeva?
explanation: Yadava Jaitugi (Jaitrapala) defeated and killed Kakatiya Rudradeva and held the young Ganapatideva captive (Hemadri; Paithan plate). Rudradeva is the victim, not the victor.

notes.text: - **Rudradeva's killer:** **Jaitugi** (APPSC PYQ) – recorded by Hemadri and confirmed by the **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra; not Narasimha Deva or Namadeva.

q: Rudramadevi's victory over the Devagiri Yadavas is recorded in which of the following inscriptions?
explanation: The Bidar fort inscription records Rudramadevi's victory over the Yadava king Mahadeva. Chandupatla records her death, Bayyaram is Mailamba's tank record and Hanumakonda is Rudradeva's 1163 record.

notes.text: - **Rudrama's victory over Mahadeva:** recorded in the **Bidar fort inscription** (APPSC PYQ) – not Bayyaram, Chandupatla or Hanumakonda.

q: The Famous king in Yadavaraja Dynasty?
explanation: Singhana (Simhana II) was the greatest Yadava king of Devagiri; Ramachandra lost to Alauddin, Bhima II was a Chaulukya and Virarajendra a Chola.

q: Who was the famous Sanskrit scholar of the Devagiri Yadava period and author of Chaturvarga Chintamani?
explanation: Hemadri, minister (Shrikaranadhipa) of the Yadavas Mahadeva and Ramachandra, wrote the Sanskrit encyclopaedia Chaturvarga Chintamani. Vidyanatha and Jayapa served the Kakatiyas, Palkuriki Somanatha was a Telugu Saiva poet.

notes.text: - **Chaturvarga Chintamani:** Sanskrit encyclopaedia by **Hemadri** (APPSC G2 2000 ×2; APPSC PYQ) – on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**; not Vidyanatha, Jayapa Senani or Palkuriki Somanatha.

q: Famous Sanskrit scholar of the time of the Devagiri Yadavas and author of Chaturvarga Chintamani?
explanation: Hemadri, the Yadava minister, wrote Chaturvarga Chintamani on dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas. Vidyanatha (Kakatiya court poet), Jayapa Senani (Nrittaratnavali) and Palkuriki Somanatha are wrong.

notes.text: - **Chaturvarga Chintamani:** Sanskrit encyclopaedia by **Hemadri** (APPSC G2 2000 ×2; APPSC PYQ) – on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**; not Vidyanatha, Jayapa Senani or Palkuriki Somanatha.

q: Who was the Raja Guru of Ganapatideva?
explanation: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Siva), head of the Golaki Matha, was Ganapatideva's raja guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet; Mallikarjuna Pandita and Sripati Pandita were Saiva teachers, not his guru.

notes.text: - **Saiva gurus:** **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva** (raja guru, APPSC PYQ ×3).

q: Kakatiyas were feudatories of which Andhra dynasty?
explanation: The Kakatiyas first appear as Rashtrakuta vassals (Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta', Garuda emblem) and later served the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

notes.text: - **First overlords:** the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 ×2; G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta", and the early emblem was **Garuda**.
- **⚠ Trap:** the **Eastern Chalukyas** only issued the Magallu grant; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

q: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?
explanation: The early Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Magallu: Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta'), then of the Kalyani Chalukyas. They were never vassals of the Yadavas, the Eastern Chalukyas or the Hoysalas.

notes.text: - **First overlords:** the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 ×2; G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta", and the early emblem was **Garuda**.
- **⚠ Trap:** the **Eastern Chalukyas** only issued the Magallu grant; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

q: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before taking over the kingdom?
explanation: The Kakatiyas were originally feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Garuda emblem) and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas (Varaha emblem). The Yadavas, Vengi Chalukyas and Hoysalas were neighbours or rivals.

notes.text: - **First overlords:** the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 ×2; G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta", and the early emblem was **Garuda**.
- **⚠ Trap:** the **Eastern Chalukyas** only issued the Magallu grant; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

q: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
explanation: The Kakatiyas were first subordinates of the Rashtrakutas, and only later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them.

notes.text: - **First overlords:** the **Rashtrakutas** (APPSC G2 2005 ×2; G2 Mains 2017 ×2) – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta", and the early emblem was **Garuda**.
- **⚠ Trap:** the **Eastern Chalukyas** only issued the Magallu grant; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

q: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
explanation: The Kakatiya rulers, as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, bore the title Mahamandaleswara (Beta II took it). It is a feudatory title, so the overlord Chalukya and Rashtrakuta kings did not use it as their style.

notes.text: - **Then:** feudatories of the **Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas** – emblem **Varaha** (changed by **Prola I**); title **Mahamandaleswara** (APPSC G2 2001), borne by Beta II.

q: Who is the Guru of Ganapati Deva?
explanation: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Sambhu) of the Golaki Matha was Ganapatideva's guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet, Palkuriki Somanatha a Virasaiva poet.

notes.text: - **Saiva gurus:** **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva** (raja guru, APPSC PYQ ×3).

q: Religious teacher of Ganapati Deva?
explanation: Visvesvara Sivacharya was Ganapatideva's guru. Rameswara Pandita was Beta II's guru and Dhruveshwara Pandita Mahadeva's.

notes.text: - **Saiva gurus:** **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva** (raja guru, APPSC PYQ ×3).

q: According to which inscription was Beta Raja-I the first Kakatiya king?
explanation: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya king. Junagadh is Rudradaman's record, Gantasala and Amaravati are Buddhist sites.

q: According to which inscription was Beta Raja I the first Kakatiya king?
explanation: The Kazipet (Dargah) inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I and names him the first Kakatiya ruler. The other inscriptions are not linked to the Kakatiya genealogy.

explanation: The Kazipet Dargah inscription traces the Kakatiya line from Beta I, naming him the first Kakatiya ruler. Junagadh, Ghantasala and Amaravati are unrelated.

q: For the first time, in which inscription were the Kakatiyas mentioned?
explanation: The Kakatiyas are first mentioned in the Magallu inscription (c. 950-956) of the Eastern Chalukya king Danarnava, through Kakatiya Gundyana. Bayyaram (13th c.) is later; Polavaram and Pillalamarri are unrelated.

q: Which inscription mentioned about Kakatiyas for the first time
explanation: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (c. 950-956) is the first mention of the Kakatiyas (Gundyana). Bayyaram is a later genealogy.

q: Who shifted the capital from Hanumakonda to Orugallu?
explanation:
Most books and keys (NextGen, Rocket, APPSC G1 2024 official match): Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Orugallu. Strictly: Rudradeva founded Orugallu and began its fort (Bekkallu inscription, 1195, already calls it his capital); Ganapatideva completed it and moved the court fully.
Ganapatideva completed the Warangal fort begun by Rudradeva and transferred the capital from Hanumakonda to Orugallu (Warangal). Rudradeva only founded the city and began the fort.

q: Who among the following bears the title 'Rayagajakesari'?
explanation: Rudramadevi took the title Rayagajakesari after driving the Yadava king Mahadeva back to Devagiri. Rudradeva was Vidyabhushana, Ganapatideva Andhra Deshadhiswara.

q: Who among the following was awarded the title 'Founder of Kakati Rajya'?
explanation:
Most books and keys: Recherla Rudra. Strictly: 'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya' was Recherla Prasaditya's title (Velugotivari Vamshavali); Recherla Rudra's were Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya / Samartha.
The Recherla family held this honour: the Velugotivari Vamshavali calls Recherla Prasaditya 'Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya', and Recherla Rudra, who saved the kingdom during Ganapati's captivity, is the Recherla general offered. Jayapa was Gajasahini, Pinachoda a Velanati chief.

q: Which of the following Kakatiya kings ruled the whole of Andhradesa as a unified sovereign, combining the Andhra, Telangana and Rayalaseema regions of present Andhra Pradesh, from Ganjam in the north to Kanchipuram in the south?
explanation: Ganapatideva (1199-1262) conquered coastal Andhra, Velanadu, Nellore and Kalinga and reached Kanchi, uniting 'Telugudesam' under one sovereign. Prataparudra I (Rudradeva) began the independent kingdom; Beta I was a feudatory.

notes.text: - **Unifier:** brought **the whole Telugu area under one rule** after the Satavahanas (1199 PYQ ×2), from Ganjam to Kanchi – the Kakatiya who ruled all Andhradesa as one sovereign (APPSC G1 2003).

q: Kakatiya king Ganapatideva ruled South India during which year?
explanation: Ganapatideva, the greatest and longest-reigning Kakatiya, ruled 1199-1262 (about 63 years). 1050-1323 spans the whole dynasty and 1411-1530 is unrelated.

notes.text: - **Reign:** **1199–1262** (about **63 years**, the longest; APPSC AE 2011); first inscription **Manthena, 26 Dec 1199**; title **Andhra Deshadhiswara**.

q: The mighty Kakatiya king who expanded his empire to Kanchi?
explanation: Ganapatideva conquered coastal Andhra, Nellore and Kalinga and his forces marched to Kanchi (Chebrolu 1228, Ganapeswaram 1231 records). Beta I, Prola I and Prola II were early feudatory rulers.

notes.text: - **Kanchi:** the most powerful Kakatiya, who **extended the empire up to Kanchi** (Group-I 1990-91; G1 1994) – not Beta I, Prola I or Prola II.

q: Who was the successor of Ganapatideva?
explanation: Ganapatideva had no son and nominated his daughter Rudramadevi as successor. Rudradeva was his uncle and predecessor's predecessor; Recherla Rudra was a general.

notes.text: - **Family:** no son → daughter **Rudramadevi succeeded him** (APPSC PYQ), raised as a son (putrika), trained by her mother **Kupama Devi**; married **Veerabhadra** of the **Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas**; daughter **Ganapamba** married the **Kota** chief; sisters **Mailamba** and **Kundamamba** married the sons of **Natavadi Buddharaja**.

q: Who defeated Ganapatideva in 1263?
explanation: In 1263 Jatavarman Sundara Pandya defeated the Kakatiya forces at Muttukur (Nellore), and Nellore passed to the Pandyas. The Velanati Chodas had already been destroyed; the Yadavas and Hoysalas did not win this battle.

q: Which of the following defeated Ganapatideva in 1263
explanation: The Pandyas under Jatavarman Sundara Pandya defeated Ganapatideva's forces at Muttukur in 1263 and took Nellore. The Velanati Chodas had ended earlier.

q: Gangadevi was a disciple of whom?
explanation: Gangadevi, wife of Kumara Kampana and author of Madhura Vijayam, hailed the Kakatiya court poet Agastya as her guru. Rameswara Pandita was Beta II's guru, Tikkana and Potana were Telugu poets.

notes.text: - **Gangadevi**, author of **Madhura Vijayam** (Vijayanagara), hailed **Agastya** as her guru; Madhura Vijayam also describes the hardship after the conquest.

q:
Assertion (A): Rudramadevi is regarded as one of the most prominent rulers of the Kakatiya dynasty.
Reason (R): From 1262 CE onwards, inscriptions began referring to Rudramadevi as a king, highlighting her authority and acceptance as a sovereign ruler.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.
key_text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
explanation:
Printed key / question: from 1262 CE. Strictly, NextGen says the inscriptions use 'Rudradeva Maharaja' from 1258 AD, during her co-regency; her sole rule dates from 1262 (NextGen Kakatiyas p.51).
Rudramadevi (reign 1262-1289) is one of the most prominent Kakatiya rulers. Her inscriptions call her 'Rudradeva Maharaja', in the male form, which shows she was accepted as a full sovereign, so R explains A.

notes.text: - **Co-regent from 1258** under the male name **Rudradeva Maharaja**; ruled to **1289**.

q: Whose daughter was Rani Rudrama Devi?
explanation: Rudrama Devi was the daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva, who had no son and trained her as heir; she ruled as Rudradeva Maharaja. Mahadeva was Ganapati's father.

notes.text: - **Daughter of Ganapatideva** and **Kupama Devi** (APPSC PYQ); Ganapati had **no son**, so she was raised as a son (**putrika**).

q: Who was the first woman to rule the Andhra region?
explanation: Rudramba (Rudramadevi, 1262-1289) was the first woman ruler of the Andhra region. Chand Bibi (Ahmadnagar) and Razia Sultana (Delhi) ruled elsewhere; Nagamma was a Palnadu minister.

notes.text: - **First woman ruler of the Andhra region** (Rudramba; APPSC PYQ); **second great woman ruler of medieval India after Razia Sultana**.

q: Rudramba (1262-1289) have Childrens?
explanation: Rudramadevi had no sons, only three daughters - Mummadamma, Rudrama and Ruyyamma; Prataparudra II was Mummadamma's son.

notes.text: - **Children:** **three daughters**, no son (APPSC Drug Inspector 2011).

q: Which inscription confirms that Rudramadevi died in Dakshinapatha Vijaya Yatra in 1289?
explanation: The Chandupatla inscription (Nalgonda), set up by her servant Puvvula Mummadi, records that Rudramadevi died in 1289 fighting the Kayastha rebel Ambadeva. The Tripurantakam inscription records Ambadeva's own victories.

notes.text: - **Chandupatla inscription** (**Nalgonda**), set up by her servant **Puvvula Mummadi**, records her death (APPSC Asst. Welfare Officers) – not Tripurantakam (Ambadeva's victories), Gurjala or Induluru.

q: Kakatiaya Rudrama had borne the title “Rayagaja Kesari " in Commemoration of her victory over:
explanation: Rudrama earned the title Rayagaja Kesari for her victory over the rulers of Devagiri (the Yadavas), whom she drove back to their capital. Her wars with the Pandyas, Kalinga Gangas and Vaidumbas did not give this title.

notes.text: - **Rayagajakesari:** title taken for her victory over the **rulers of Devagiri** (Yadava **Mahadeva**, chased back to Devagiri) (APPSC G2 PYQ ×3) – not the Pandyas, Kalinga rulers or Vaidumbas.

q: Who among the following used the title 'Rayagaja Kesari'
explanation: Rayagajakesari was the title of Rudramadevi, earned by her victory over the Yadavas of Devagiri. Rudradeva, Ganapatideva and Prataparudra bore other titles.
